What the debugger's CPU log (`LOG`, `LOGS`, `LOGL`, `LOGC`) and the terminal around it produced
on live DOSBox-X sessions, captured on 2026-10-01 with `dosbox-x --version` 2026.08.31 (the
Homebrew build, heavy debug), headless, every session started with
`flags=["-set", "cpu core=normal"]` unless a name says `dynamic` (`cpu core=dynamic`). A script
drove this server in process: each `LOG` command typed at a stop as `trace` types it (its count
in hex, one more than the instructions it executes), the stop heard by the prompt, every
`Session._read` chunk of that wait recorded after the ANSI strip and joined (`*-delta.txt`), the
`BPLIST` survey before and after it (`*-survey-*.txt`), and the `LOGCPU.TXT` the debugger wrote
(`*.trace`), moved out of the working directory at once. Nothing here is authored: the tests
replay these files, and where a test needs a case no capture holds it changes one field of one of
them and says which.
Program and board names were then replaced by neutral labels by a single mechanical substitution
that preserves every field width; nothing else was edited.

<bench>-<shape>-64.trace   64 instructions in each shape (65 lines, the last the stop), the stop
                           read off the pane after each run:
  probe-settle-*           the package's probe guest (probe.conf), at its settle `loop`, 0814:0106;
                           each stopped at 0814:0106
  dos-real16-*                 dos-real16 (TMP/dosbox-mcp.conf, program ..\exes\real16.exe), at
                           COMPOSE_FRAME, 15A3:0000, real mode, map loaded at segment 0892; each
                           stopped at 15A3:003C
  dos-djgpp32-*                 dos-djgpp32 (build/mcp.conf, DJGPP32.EXE D:\MIDI\TUNE00.MID -a), at
                           _engine_pos, 00A7:0005E9C0, Pr32 paged, DJGPP32.SYM based off CS, each
                           from its own _engine_pos stop: normal stopped at 00A7:0003D451, short at
                           00A7:00060D71, long at 00A7:001604C0, cs_ip at 00A7:00028DCF
dos-real16-compose-cs_ip-500.trace   500 instructions from COMPOSE_FRAME, `LOGC 1F5`
probe-start-long-200.trace       200 instructions from `start` (0814:010B), `LOGL C9`

The doubles' scenarios, each a survey before, the command's delta, the trace, a survey after:
  probe-settle-cs_ip-16    `LOGC 11` at the settle loop; `cc=` 192333 -> 192349
  probe-settle-normal-16   `LOG 11` right after it; `cc=` 192349 -> 192365
  probe-dynamic-cs_ip-16   `LOGC 11` on the dynamic core at the settle loop; `cc=` 238 -> 238
  probe-cut-*              a breakpoint at 0814:0108, then `LOGC 186A1` from ECX 1582: the stop at
                           0108 with the log open (`probe-cut-open.trace`, copied while open; no
                           `created` in its delta), then `LOGC 0`, which closed it executing
                           nothing and left the same bytes; `cc=` 192365 -> 197871 -> 197871
  probe-start-normal-200   `LOG C9` from `start`; `cc=` 19663481 -> 19663681
  dos-djgpp32-engine-cs_ip-200  `LOGC C9` from _engine_pos; `cc=` 1963039200 -> 1963039400; the
                           `GDT` and `LDT` listings read off the session's logfile at that stop
                           (`dos-djgpp32-gdt-listing.txt`, `dos-djgpp32-ldt-listing.txt`). The join's double
                           answers `CPU` from `../machine/dos-djgpp32-CPU.log.txt`, the same program in
                           the same mode at another stop: only the mode it states is read
dos-djgpp32-engine.sym          the rows of that build's `build/DJGPP32.SYM` that place the window: for
                           each address, the nearest symbol at or below it and its two neighbours,
                           section names (`.text` and the like) left out as `symbols_load` leaves
                           them out; copied as `nm` printed them

Then in the order the tool makes them since, the log moved out BEFORE `LOGC 0`, on the probe
guest with `BPINT 21` armed:
  probe-post-*             `LOGC 186A1` from the park at the reset vector: the BIOS's power-on
                           self test closed the log (`cpu log LOGCPU.TXT stopped` in the log) after
                           3 lines, and the machine ran on to an INT 21 at F000:DAC6; `cc=` 0 ->
                           318. `LOGC 0` then wrote a fresh empty file (`probe-post-close.trace`)
  probe-int-at-*           `LOGC 186A1` started on that INT 21: one line, the INT, counted by
                           `cc=` (318 -> 319) and not executed, the stop at the same place; the
                           close wrote no file
  probe-int-mid-*          a step past it, `BPINT 21` armed again, `LOGC 186A1`: 7 lines, the last
                           the next INT 21 at 0814:0108, `cc=` 320 -> 327; the close wrote no file

Three more, from live sessions of the same build on the same day that drove this server's own
`trace` on the probe guest:
  probe-on-bp-cs_ip.trace  `trace(100000, cs_ip)` started on an armed code breakpoint at 0814:0108:
                           one line, that address, nothing executed, `OTHER_STOP` attributed to it
  probe-post-logfile.txt   the session's logfile lines `trace(16, cs_ip, seconds=5)` from the reset
                           park produced: the log started, then closed by the power-on self test
  probe-count-logfile.txt  the session's logfile lines `trace(16, cs_ip)` produced at the settle
                           loop, a log that ran out at its count

And one from a live session of the same build on 2026-10-02 that drove `Session.log_cpu` in process
on a copy of the probe guest whose working directory was set to mode 0555 at the settle loop:
  probe-unwritable-*       `LOGC 11` typed there: the delta, ending at the prompt with `LOGC 11`
                           still on the input line, the guest never released and no LOGCPU.TXT
                           made; and the session's logfile lines it wrote, `Starting log`,
                           `Logfile couldn't be created.` and `command not recognized`. Every
                           command typed after it in that session wrote those three lines again,
                           and `BPLIST` printed no list. The survey before it is
                           `probe-settle-survey-before.txt`'s, the same stop on the same build
